articleTitle: Keynote Speaker
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Provides an abstract of the keynote presentation and may include a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Vision Based Detection and Classification of Disease on Rice Crops Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: This paper presents a combination of K-mean s clustering, SVM and CNN based classification techniques for the crop disease / infection with target as Rice crop. Agricultural crops show variation in features of healthy crops in color, texture and growth. Manual inspection and monitoring of crops is incompatible for large farm sizes so aerial monitoring or camera imaging can prove to be helpful for agriculturists in pre-determination of crop diseases. The use of image processing algorithms involving K-means clustering, Support vector machine and Convolutional Neural Networks enables classification process. The supervised classification techniques involve prior training process which determines the accuracy. The training dataset involved initially with 10 image set which was increased to over 50 to obtain accuracy over 95 percent.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Double Gate Heterojunction Tunnel Field Effect Transistor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: In this paper, we have done the comparison of the performance of various TFET devices like Single gated, double gated, Homojunction and the Heterojunction. All the simulations have been performed on Cogenda Software. The analysis have been done in terms of I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub>/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub> ratio and subthreshold swing parameters. The results show improvements in ON current by using double gated TFET structure (1.5 times more than the single gated TFET) and heterojunction structure (57 times more than the single gated TFET).

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Transport Layer Congestion Control Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Internet applications are increasing network traffic exponentially these days due to remarkable growth of the Internet. To handle the huge traffic on Transport Layer one provides the most trusted, Connection oriented and end-to-end packet delivery protocol which is Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). There are many problems available in congestion control algorithms i.e. transfer size of the packet, initialization of Congestion Window, cross traffic, congestion along the path, size of the router buffer, intra protocol and inter protocol fairness. There are many variants of the protocol available to control the congestion. This paper presents a comparative analysis of commonly used TCP flavors. We present analysis of TCP protocol named, TCP Reno, CUBIC-TCP, FAST-FIT, TCP New Reno and followed by experiment results.

articleTitle: Impact of Gate Dielectric on Drain Current, Gate Capacitance and Trans-conductance for MOSFET, Nanowire FET and CNTFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Semiconductor Nanowires (NWs) as well as Carbon Nanotubes (CNT) areeye-catching components for forthcoming electronics, as they can demonstrate a variety of device characteristics and also work as bridging wires that link to large scale metallization. The impact of variation in gate dielectric upon gate capacitance as well as drain current and trans-conductance for single and double gate MOSFET, silicon nanowire FET along with carbon nanotube FET devices has been studied. It was observed that once a high k dielectric is use up CNTFET and silicon nanowire FET show lower quantum capacitance, higher drain current and almost same trans-conductance.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Metrics for Safeguarding the Performance of Data Centre Communication Systems by Green Cloud Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Cloud computing involves sharing of the reservoir containing resources of computation for data centres whenever demanded. Proficiency in a data centre, is a core requirement to be achieved. To attain the highest performance and efficiency levels the consumption of energy also increases simultaneously. This increased energy consumption is associated with untoward side-effects like heat & carbon emissions. Hence we have to proceed with an objective of highest performance and energy efficiency with least associated side-effects to avoid the environmental threat of global warming and raised carbon footprint levels. These parameters are achieved to a great extent by application of suitable metrics on the cloud computing platform. These metrics mainly focus on the objectives as to how to enhance the IT tools and systems power proficiency. The metrics discussed in this paper resolve this problem to a great extent. None of the metrics proposed is singularly capable of performance and energy enhancement. Therefore the metrics in consideration are collectively utilized for improving performance of communication systems of data-centres. These metrics are tested on four different architectures viz. DCell, BCube, Hypercube and Fat tree three-tier.

articleTitle: Automated Ensembling of Features from Android Applications for Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Android malwares are proliferating in the public spaces like never before. The urge of the adversaries to collect user data through various means to establish a pattern or behaviour is ever growing. The malwares have become sophisticated to label them as good or bad. In this paper, we try to establish a good set of features from Android applications to label them as benign or malware. We have developed a framework to automatically extract features via stationary, static and dynamic analysis of the Android applications. Pre-static analysis include application meta-data from playstore and Android manifest from application. Static analysis of the application comprises flow-droid's source-sink identification, api to permission mapping and n-gram statistical analysis. Dynamic analysis of the application is performed using Google's droidbox and monitoring the system calls. The features are exported in a general format and can act a input to a learning based model for application classification.

articleTitle: Gate Length Modulation of Junction-less Transistor Based on Silicon Nanowire
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Here we have simulated the influence on the characteristics of Silicon Nanowire Junction-less transistor (JLT) with help of PADRE MuGFET simulation tools in the situation when we vary the length of gate. We noticed that when welength of gate was changed, the corresponding characteristics changed in accordance with it. We have examined this change by analyzing different output parameters which includes its transfer characteristics, transconductance, Drain Induced Barrier Lowering (DIBL) effect, electric potential, the value of threshold voltage and electric field of the device. We have results which shows that when we increase the length of gate, the value of the current decrease keeping gat voltage (Vg) at 0V. The value range of parameters like electric potential and electric field increased while there was a drop in threshold voltage. The peak of transconductance started reaching new heights but the observations in DIBL effect was just opposite. From the simulations we got to know that use of devices with smaller length of gates should be preferable as the results were better with them.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Fuzzy Control Base for Single Axis Active Magnetic Bearing System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: These days Active Magnetic Bearing (AMB) is an exceptionally propelled territory of research and their applications are progressive. Despite the fact that AMBs are very non-linear and open loop unstable framework, the utilization of controllers influences them to work legitimately and stable. Controllers that have been utilizing for AMB are for the most part traditional or, customary one which comprises an issue of tuning as the rotor position get somewhat changed. In this paper, a Fuzzy logic controller (FLC) is imitated in the Fuzzy logic tool of MATLAB to play out the controller activity of the proposed AMB framework. As the situation of the rotor gets changed FLC consequently control the framework which takes out the manual tuning activity when contrasted with the traditional controller. Further, the FLC controlled AMB is observed for stability and the transient response is additionally observed by varying the rotor position from 2mm to 20mm.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Evaluation of Disaster Relief
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Ad hoc networks are considered more suitable for disaster scenarios due to infrastructure-less feature. Existing routing algorithms used on such mobile ad hoc networks are non-adaptive routing algorithms and based on shortest path algorithms. But shortest path may not give optimum path. If the network is heavy loaded with traffic, shortest path may not give better results. Various reinforcement algorithms are used to design such adaptive routing where the routing takes place based on the actual traffic present on a network. One of the reinforcement routing algorithms is Q routing and various variants of Q routing like CQ routing, CDRQ routing etc. In this paper, Q routing and CDRQ routing are implemented and compared using disaster area mobility model in disaster area scenario.

articleTitle: State Estimation of a Quantum System Using Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: In this paper we propose to estimate the state of a quantum system dynamically evolving in the presence of white Gaussian noise (WGN) under Schrödinger dynamics using Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm. In the proposed measurement model the EKF is applied to obtain the conditional expectation of the state at a given observation time up to that time. First the complex Schrödinger equation of dimension N is transformed into a real Schrödinger equation of dimension 2N. MATLAB programs were implemented to plot the wave function, error and noise to signal ratio (NSR). NSR within minimum bounds is obtained.

articleTitle: Vehicle Overloading Alert using IoT
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is a new technology which has made human life easier for automation. There is a use of various sensors inbuilt in the systems for various automation purpose. These sensors play a vital role in detecting and hence alarming us about a particular consequence. In the present era, it has been noticed that everyone is indulged in money making without thinking about consequences. In the Transportation Industry, this practice has taken the shape of overloading. Although there are many rules, its effective implementation requires an organized system. Keeping a view on the current scenario, this paper proposes a set of ideas and measures to be adopted that measures the overload and alert and if it is ignored the vehicle information is forwarded to check-posts so that any severe accidents can be prevented coming their way. The overloading is detected with the use of Wifi Weight sensors and the collected data is compared with the data in the database corresponding to the probable paths to alarm about the overloading and if it is ignored then it would notify the concerned authorities.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Coin Matching Using Local Texture Features
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: At present coin recognition and classification tasks are performed manually by the numismatists. This process requires lot of time and proper preservation of hard copies of source documents such as printed catalog. Hence automation in this area is very much helpful and supportive. In this paper machine vision based automatic coin recognition using local texture features such as SIFT (Scale Invariant Feature Transform) and SURF (Speed Up Robust Features) algorithms are proposed to complement the conventionalmanual classification and recognition process. This work is carried out on ancient Roman coins and the performance is compared.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Based Optimal Scheduling of Microgrid Considering Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: This paper proposes a multi-objective based optimal scheduling methodology for a Microgrid (MG) including diesel generators, solar PV, wind generators, demand response (DR), battery energy storage systems (BESSs) and electric vehicles (EVs), Different uncertainties exist in the microgrids, and they are mainly caused by intermittent output power of non-dispatchable renewable power generation such as solar PV and wind power outputs. Power outputs from solar PV, wind, BESSs and EVs are modeled, and their uncertainties are handled by considering the probability analysis. Here, the operating cost of MG and amount of emission released are considered as two objectives to be optimized for the optimal scheduling of MG considering uncertainties. The operating cost minimization objective is formulated by incorporating the cost due to power to/from main grid and MG, diesel generators, solar PV, wind units, EVs, BESSs, and DR. First, these two objectives are optimized independently by using enhanced genetic algorithm (EGA), and then they are optimized simultaneously by using nondominated sorting genetic algorithm-II. Simulations are carried out on a test Microgrid system by including all the MG components, single and multiple objectives.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Approach to Select Most Suitable Conflict Resolution Strategy in Multi-Agent System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Selection of a suitable conflict resolution strategy depends on conflict type, degree of assertiveness of agents and agent's concern. The state of the art in conflict resolution ignores the factors like the agent's level of concern for self and others. The criteria for classification of the factors affecting the selection of a conflict resolution strategy is also too theoretical that divides the conflict strength and confidence level of conflicting agents into `High' and `Low' exactly at the center of the range resulting in abrupt change in selection of conflict resolution strategy at margins. In this paper, the use of fuzzy logic to select the most suitable conflict resolution strategy for software agents is proposed that is comprehensive and tries to improvise quality within cost constraints.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of PQIACS
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: A performance comparison between without bridge single ended primary inductance converter (SEPIC) and without bridge Zeta converter based air conditioning system (ACS) is presented in this paper. In the presented models, dc motor at the output is controlled by an electronic commutation switching. The power factor at the utility side is improved using these without bridge converter configurations which are operating in discontinuous mode of inductor current. The performance of both the ACSs are analyzed and further compared to select the optimal configuration for a specific case, with power quality improvement that adheres the guidelines of international standard.

articleTitle: E-Governance Initiatives and Challenges in the State of Uttar Pradesh
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: E-governance has emerged as an important field in India which deals with the service governed by the government for everyone in open network. The e-governance can make governance more efficient and effective and also brings other benefits to the citizens. Right from its inspections the Union government and states have been working together to provide various information and services to the users. It has been realized by all stack-holders that it has potential to let the citizen access and connect to government and its services without involvement of the middleman. This paper outlines and explains various e-governance projects of UP Government. It also discusses the challenges and issues faced by government and citizens.

articleTitle: Recurrent Convolutional Attention Neural Model for Sentiment Classification of short text
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Nowadays neural attention model doing good in many tasks of natural language processing (NLP). More specifically attention mechanism has been used widely with convolutional neural network (CNN) and recurrent neural network (RNN) for many task of NLP. But the sentiment classification of short text is a challenging task because it contains limited contextual information. Thus, we proposed a new recurrent convolutional attention neural model for sentiment classification of the short text by using attention mechanism with RCNN (recurrent convolutional neural network). In proposed model attention score is calculated by averaging hidden units (feature maps) generated from LSTM (long short-term memory). Then we combined this attention score with recurrent convolution-based encoded text features to get final sentence representation. Here attention will focus on important text features and recurrent convolution makes full use of limited contextual information by processing sentence representation through different windows sizes with specialized recurrent convolution operation. Validation of the proposed model is done through experimentation with three benchmark datasets i.e. MR, SSTl, and SST2. Achieved results exhibit that our model performs better than many existing baselines works on all three datasets.

articleTitle: Performance and Emission Analysis of CI Engine Fuelled with Blend of Jatropha Biodiesel and ZnO Nanoparticles as Fuel Additives
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: In current scenario the biggest problem of the developing countries is the source of the energy. Countries like India and china importing the petroleum product from petroleum producing countries. Both countries spend lot money to import the fuel. Now a days developing country are investing to bring a better solution of diesel and petrol. The current study deals with the production of biodiesel from jatropha and these jatropha oil biodiesel are blended in diesel at different concentration (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%) and B20% blend was enriched with ZnO nano particle at different concentration (50, 100, 150, 200 ppm). These blends are analyzed for their chemical properties and performance. Density, flashpoint, kinematic viscosity increases with the increase of the concentration of the both biodiesel and the ZnO nano particle. In performance test all the emissions are decrease with the increases of biodiesel and ZnO nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Inference System based Fault Detection in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: A novel method of fault detection in smart grid is proposed in this paper. The proposed method is based on Fuzzy Inference System, where the Mamdani approach has been considered to determine the estimated failure time prevailing in a smart grid system during a faulty condition. A prototype model of three phase distribution system has been developed. The model has arbitrarily been subjected to different faults like Line-to-Line fault, Line-to-Ground fault etc. and the fault current index under each condition has been obtained using the concept of System Average Interruption Duration Index. One of the significant parameters of analysis of failure time during a faulty condition System is Interruption Duration Index. A study of various unplanned conditions has been performed that can prevail during fault. Ageing of the setup when the existing system is upgraded into a smart grid system may lead to significant reduction in efficiency of the system and hence affect the self-healing process of Smart grid system. Effect of temperature during occurrence of fault has also been taken into account which arises due to significant carbon absorption rise and may influence the performance of the system. The numerical results demonstrate that with the variation in dissimilar input, there can be diverse conditions which are situation dependent. When predicted and unpredicted conditions are taken into consideration the clearance time of fault in such situations can be identify beforehand which helps in making the system more reliable and resilient when concentrated in a smart grid system.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Control Strategy for Maximum Power Point Tracking of Variable Speed Wind Turbine using Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Variability in the wind speed necessitates the use of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of wind energy conversion systems to harvest maximum power that is optimally suited for the user loads. Commonly used Incremental Conductance (INC) algorithm has shown poor tracking performance under unpredictable and changing environmental conditions. In this paper a model predictive technique is used with conventional Incremental Conductance MPPT to improve tracking performance of wind energy conversion system. MPC predicts the estimates of control variables one step ahead into the time horizon and actuates switching signal to achieve desired cost function. This technique improves tracking performance and power harvesting capability compared to conventional Incremental Conductance (INC) MPPT under wide range of wind speed variations. Performance of the proposed MPC MPPT is analyzed using MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation study.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of FinFET based Temperature Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: In this VLSI era, integrated circuit designing has attained new trends. With the scaling technology the feature size have reached below 40nm in implementation. With such a huge component density over a small die heat dissipation analysis is important. There is a need to develop and monitor temperature for all the components over IC. The paper represents the design and simulation of FinFET based temperature sensor. The sensor is designed in Symica EDA tool using FinFET on 32nm feature and uses 1.2 volts as a supply voltage. This circuit is used for sensing the temperature and it has one PNP transistor and two FinFET and generates the complementary to absolute temperature (CTAT) voltage simulated over temperature range from -20°c to + 120°c.

articleTitle: Unfolding design strategies and the critical aspects for development of DAQ at the HEP experiments
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to illustrate the decisive aspects to be taken care during the DAQ development for HEP experiments. The extensive design strategies are explored along with the consideration for the efficient data transfer. The results highlights the advantages of the devised FPGA based readout approach over the conventional methodologies along with the pursued data formats.

articleTitle: Wide-band CPW-Fed Slotted Rectangular Patch Antenna loaded with Ring Resonators for C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: A new design of wide-band, co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed, rectangular patch antenna loaded with continuous ring resonators (RPACRR) is proposed for C-band. The proposed RPACRR design consisted top layer of optimized rectangular patches of copper with 0.035 mm thickness, middle layer of FR-4 substrate of thickness 2 mm and the bottom layer of concentric continuous ring resonators (CCRRs) of 0.035 mm. The proposed RPACRR design with dimensions 33.30 mm × 20.22 mm × 2 mm is simulated in two different configurations, with CCRRs and without CCRRs. The simulated results for RPACRR design showed transmission peaks at 3.9 GHz and 5.4 GHz with reflection coefficients of -15.42 dB and -23.01 dB simultaneously. The uniqueness in the design is CPW line, consisting of rectangular patches and replacement of ground patch layer with patches of CCRRs that act as defective ground layer. The combined resonance effect of patch antenna backed by CCRRs resulted in broad-band of 3.53 GHz. The proposed RPACRR design exhibited broad-band transmission band-width that resonates at frequencies lying in C-band with potential application in wireless communication.

articleTitle: Designing of Vapour Cycle Cooling System of Twin Seater Basic Trainer Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: This paper presents designing of Vapour Cycle Cooling System (VCCS) for twin seater basic trainer aircraft for Cockpit Air Conditioning. Design specification calls for maintaining cabin mean temperature of 26°C and 50% RH at ambient temperature 40°C & speed 0.4 Mach. Maximum cockpit heat load including condenser & evaporator fan heat loads is estimated as 6.5 KW. At this heat load, to maintain cabin mean temperature of 26°C, there is a need to supply 831.5Kg/hr of air flow into cockpit at a temperature of 5°C. This envisaged VCCS evaporator heat load 8.14 KW as ambient air is sucked by evaporator fan at 40°C. VCCS design calculations with R134fa refrigerant have been carried out in iterative process for final selection of evaporator temperature of -6°C, condenser temperature 60°C with 5°C superheat & compressor work <; 4.8 KW. Control logics have been developed to control the VCCS in all flight regimes.

articleTitle: Vegetable Classification Using You Only Look Once Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Vegetable detection and classification is a challenging objective in daily production and use, and the complexity increases when other parameters such as shape, size and color are taken into consideration. In this paper, we define a methodology that will detect and classify three different green vegetables of different sizes. This method involves the use of Tensor Flow, Dark flow which is a Tensor flow version of You only look once (YOLO) algorithm, OpenCV. To train the desired network, several various vegetable images were fed into the network. The images were pre-processed before training by drawing bounding boxes around the vegetable manually using OpenCV. The main algorithm responsible for the detection and classification is YOLO. This method provides a faster and smarter way to identify an object in the given image or video. Once the network is trained, the test input is passed in to the network. Once the input is provided to the network, the output will display bounding boxes around the recognized vegetable and label it with its predicted class category with accuracy of 61.6 percent.

articleTitle: Automated Image Splicing Detection using Texture based Feature Criterion and Fuzzy Support Vector Machine based Classifier
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Nowadays manipulation in digital image becomes quite simple and convenient with the broad use of advanced image editing software and the recognition of forged region cannot be captured by naked human eyes easily. One of the most frequent alterations apply on the images is called image splicing, which consists of cropping a region from an image and paste it onto a different image in order to alter the information present in the new source. There are various methodologies which address this kind of attack, by dividing the image into blocks in an attempt to detect the inconsistencies created by the attack. Though features can be edges, corners, blobs or characteristics of noise changes, alteration in illumination acquired throughout the image. Moreover image splicing is quite harder to identify tampering in a forged image. In this paper the methodology used for splicing detection is relied on texture based features which are extracted from the tampered and actual images in the form of Grey Level Run Length Matrix calculated in four directions. The features have demonstrated the potential of proposed methodology used for identification of image forgery. Thereafter fuzzy support vector machine is utilized as a new classification technique with the high generalization capability. More effective methodology is proposed for detection of splicing forgery and produced improved classification outputs.

articleTitle: Investigating the Possibility to Extend Planar Technology to 10 nm Scale with UTBB DMG SSOI MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Nowadays, ultrathin body-and-BOX (UTBB) and back-gate (BG) biasing are becoming very popular tools in strengthening the implementation of CMOS technology below 22 nm technology node. The present report provides some in-depth design guidelines to optimize the performance of UTBB strained-Si-on-insulator (SSOI) MOSFETs with the help of dual-metal-gate (DMG) accompanied by back-gate (BG) control. The dual-metal-gate (DMG) electrode, on one hand, boosts up the transport efficiency in the channel region and reduces the hot-carrier effects (HCEs) as well. On the other hand, the back-gate biasing competently suppresses short-channel effects (SCEs) with amplified scaling opportunities. The optimization of device parameters is done up to 10 nm channel length with acceptable subthreshold swing, SCEs and drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL) by using the ultra-thin BOX for enhancing back gate controllability with lightly doped drain (LDD). The present appraisal of device characteristics is based on numerical simulations carried out comprehensively on two-dimensional device simulator ATLAS™ by Silvaco Int.

articleTitle: Conjecture of Scholars Academic Performance using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Machine learning is one of the pioneer approaches to harness accurate relevant details from the complex datasets. Because of highly advanced and efficient computational and storage capabilities - this approach is best suited for several real world applications like analyzing students' performance. The paper's scope is to investigate the academic performance of the students on the basis of their end-semester marks and whether they have any back papers. The paper summarizes the qualitative comparison of several machine learning algorithms so that on the basis of a given problem statement - best suited and efficient algorithm can be opted to get optimum performance.

articleTitle: Smart Cards with Biometric Influences: An Enhanced ID Authentication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Cutting-edge Technologies in Engineering (ICon-CuTE)
abstract: Management of flow of all kinds of objects including human beings signifies their real time monitoring. This paper outlines the advantages accrued out of biometrics integration with Smartcards. It showcases the identity authentication employed through different biometric techniques. Biometric key considerations influencing the essence of this technology in Smartcards have been discussed briefly in this paper. With better accuracy and highly reliable support system this technology finds itself today in widespread deployment. However, there are still some concerns with human interfaces along with important factors in implementations of biometrics with smartcards which have been highlighted in this article. This paper also examines the privacy concerns of users in addressing their apprehensions to protect their confidentiality through biometric encryption and proposes DNA technology as a best possible biometric solution. However, due to inherent limitations of its processing time and an instant requirement of authentication, it has been suggested in the proposed modal to use it with combination of one or more suitable biometric technologies. An instant access has been proposed to the user with limited rights by using biometric technology other than the DNA as a primary source of authentication. DNA has been proposed as secondary source of authentication where only after due sample comparison full access rights to the user will be granted. This paper also aims in highlighting the number of advantages offered by the integration of biometrics with smartcards. It also discusses the need to tackle existing challenges due to restrictions in processing of different biometric technologies by defining certain specific future scopes for improvements in existing biometric technologies mainly against the time taken by it for sample comparisons.
